package_info.package_manager: N/A (browser-based exploit, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Affects web applications that are frameable and browsers (e.g., Chrome 91.0.4472.101, Edge 91.0.864.37, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The exploit leverages browser history stack manipulation via iframes to infer authentication state or other sensitive information about users on third-party sites, violating the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) and enabling cross-site information disclosure and user tracking.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a malicious site)
required_permissions: ability to load third-party sites in iframes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code repeatedly loads a restricted page from a target site in an iframe, measures the browser's history stack length before and after, and infers the user's authentication state based on whether the stack length increases, enabling cross-site information disclosure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code attempts to infer sensitive authentication state from another origin by abusing browser history stack behavior, which is not intended to be accessible cross-origin.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web applications do not attempt to measure or infer authentication state of users on other origins via history stack manipulation. SOP is expected to prevent such cross-origin information leaks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may use iframes for embedding content, but not for probing authentication state of other sites.
key_indicators: Repeatedly loading a restricted page from another origin in an iframe
Measuring and comparing history.length to infer cross-origin state
Writing authentication status to the DOM based on history stack changes

attack_chain.action: Victim visits a malicious website controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious site loads target site in an iframe.

attack_chain.action: Malicious site loads a restricted page from the target site in an iframe and records the initial history stack length.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repeated iframe reloads and history stack measurements.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code repeatedly sets the iframe src to the restricted page, triggering possible redirects (e.g., to login page if not authenticated).
attack_chain.leads_to: History stack length changes depending on authentication state.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code compares the saved and current history stack lengths to infer if the user is authenticated on the target site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker learns sensitive cross-site information (authentication state).

behavioral_signatures: Repeated iframe loads of the same cross-origin restricted page
JavaScript code measuring and comparing window.history.length
DOM updates or network requests based on history stack differences
file_indicators: Presence of iframes with src attributes set to external/restricted URLs
JavaScript accessing or comparing window.history.length in conjunction with iframe manipulation
network_indicators: Multiple requests to the same restricted resource from a single page via iframes
Unusual patterns of iframe-based navigation to authentication or protected endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web pages that embed external sites in iframes and use JavaScript to access or compare window.history.length, especially in conjunction with repeated iframe src changes targeting authentication or restricted resources. Flag sites that update the DOM or send network requests based on history stack differences as potential XSHM exploit attempts.
